C-SESSION-WRITE-ATOMICITY.IntentSummary: Make the persisted session profile one all-or-nothing backend transaction: a new mt_prefs_set_many command applies the four lastSession* keys (lastSessionTabs, lastSessionActive, lastSessionFolders, lastSessionFormats) under one PrefsState mutex acquisition and one PrefsStore::save(), so the existing temp-sibling + sync_all + rename atomicity that already protects the single store file covers the whole profile and every on-disk state is one complete generation, never a torn mix of two generations. Quarantine a corrupt profile store honestly on read — the corrupt preferences.json is renamed to a stable quarantined sibling (m068 move-aside precedent) before the empty-defaults fallback, preserving the evidence instead of letting the next save silently overwrite it. Bound the window-close wait on the in-flight session write: the renderer close path (editor.js's prepareCommit arm for quit/window-close) races the profile write against a fixed two-second timer; on confirmation the close proceeds after the write settled, on timeout or write rejection the close still proceeds with a logged BLOCK marker — the save can delay the close at most two seconds, never block it forever. Surface the session write's rejection instead of swallowing it: _saveSessionState replaces the four sequential ipcPrefs.set(...).catch(() => {}) calls with one batched write whose rejection propagates to the callers, while the Promise.allSettled per-tab position flushes keep their current ordering and always run. Profile content schema is unchanged (same four keys, same value shapes, readable by the current RESTORE_SESSION and the cold-start offer); mt_prefs_get/mt_prefs_set/mt_prefs_get_all keep their semantics with mt_prefs_set remaining the canonical single-key surface; the m001 close state machine, prevent_close handoff, mt_close_window destroy and the debounced 400 ms autosave boot gate are unchanged.

T-001.Title: M-005 batch command: mt_prefs_set_many applies the session profile under one mutex acquisition and one atomic save, with an injected-rename one-transaction pin

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Failing-first proof precedes implementation: the new pins below are added and shown red on the delivery baseline (the batch command absent, the four-key profile writable only as four separate transactions) before the implementation lands; the red run must demonstrate the current torn-profile window — a mid-sequence stop between two per-key writes leaves two generations on disk with no error surfaced.

src-tauri/src/m005_prefs.rs gains a serde wire struct PrefsEntry { key: String, value: Value } and a PrefsState::set_many(&self, entries: Vec<PrefsEntry>) -> Result<(), std::io::Error> that takes the store mutex exactly once, inserts every entry, and runs guard.save() exactly once — no intermediate save, no per-key flush, no lock release between inserts — so the whole profile becomes one temp+sync_all+rename transaction. A new #[tauri::command] pub async fn mt_prefs_set_many(entries: Vec<PrefsEntry>, app: tauri::AppHandle, prefs: State<'_, PrefsState>) -> Result<(), String> applies the batch through set_many, maps the io error to String for the caller, and preserves the mt_prefs_set broadcast semantics once per batch: after the single save it emits the full snapshot on mt::user-preference to every webview window with the existing [Prefs][broadcast] logging shape (BLOCK_EMIT_FAILED on emit failure, BLOCK_FANOUT count) — one broadcast, not four. mt_prefs_get, mt_prefs_set and mt_prefs_get_all keep their exact current bodies and semantics; ordinary single-key preference writes do not migrate to the batch command.

src-tauri/src/main.rs registers the new command in invoke_handler as m005_prefs::mt_prefs_set_many, placed immediately after the existing m005_prefs::mt_prefs_set, line — registration only, no other main.rs change.

Injection seam per the m068 promote_staging_over_live precedent: the body of PrefsStore::save() moves into a private save_with_rename(&self, rename: &dyn Fn(&Path, &Path) -> std::io::Result<()>) -> Result<(), std::io::Error> (identical steps: create_dir_all, .tmp sibling, write_all, sync_all, injected rename over the canonical name, BLOCK_PERSISTED log), save() delegates to save_with_rename(fs::rename), and a #[cfg(test)] PrefsState::set_many_with_rename(entries, rename) mirrors set_many with the injected rename so tests can fail the rename without touching the production path. Every existing call site behavior is byte-equivalent.

Inline #[cfg(test)] pins, failing-first: set_many_writes_session_profile_in_one_transaction — seed a previous generation (a set of a non-session key plus distinct lastSession* values), snapshot the raw file bytes, run set_many (or set_many_with_rename with a counting rename closure) carrying all four lastSession* keys, and prove the counting closure recorded exactly ONE rename invocation, the on-disk file contains the complete new generation (all four keys present, previous values replaced), and a fresh PrefsState::from_path reads every key back; set_many_failure_keeps_previous_generation_and_never_promotes_tmp — the same seed, then set_many_with_rename with an always-failing rename closure: the error is returned to the caller, the live file bytes are still exactly the previous generation, no partial or mixed content appears, and the .tmp sibling never became the live file. The existing save_is_atomic, persistence_across_reloads, set_get_roundtrip, prefs_store_save_roundtrip_writes_pretty_json and follow_system_theme_true_survives_reload pins keep passing with UNCHANGED bodies.

Synchronize the file-local GRACE markup in src-tauri/src/m005_prefs.rs: the MODULE_CONTRACT SCOPE sentence records the batch command and the quarantine-on-load behavior (T-002 lands the quarantine text), and a dated 2026-11-21 C-SESSION-WRITE-ATOMICITY CHANGE_SUMMARY entry names the batch transaction, the PrefsEntry wire shape and the one-broadcast fanout; no unrelated markup edits.

T-002.Title: M-005 quarantine-on-load: a corrupt preferences.json is moved aside to a stable sibling with its bytes preserved before the empty-defaults fallback

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Failing-first proof precedes implementation: corrupt_store_file_is_quarantined_aside_not_overwritten is added and shown red on the baseline (the corrupt file stays in place with no quarantined sibling) before the quarantine lands.

PrefsStore::load_from quarantines before falling back: on every corrupt branch (parse failure, non-object root, non-NotFound io error) the store attempts one fs::rename of the unreadable file to a stable quarantined sibling derived from the file name — preferences.json becomes preferences.json.corrupt in the same directory (a with_file_name/format!("{}.corrupt") derivation; never a path built from store data) — before the existing Map::new() empty-defaults return. On rename success the [Prefs][load] marker family gains BLOCK_PREFS_QUARANTINED naming the quarantine sibling by file name only (no absolute paths in the new diagnostic fields — the safe_eprintln BLOCK_* convention with the existing [Prefs] prefix); on rename failure it logs BLOCK_PREFS_QUARANTINE_FAILED with the error and still proceeds to empty defaults — quarantine failure never blocks boot or panics. The NotFound first-launch branch keeps BLOCK_FIRST_LAUNCH and performs no quarantine. The corrupt bytes are therefore preserved for diagnosis instead of being silently overwritten by the next save.

Expectation updates on the two existing corrupt pins keep every current assertion that still holds and add the quarantine expectation without weakening the empty-defaults behavior: corrupt_json_falls_back_to_empty keeps asserting the empty store and that a subsequent set writes a valid file readable at the canonical path, and additionally asserts the .corrupt sibling exists carrying the exact original garbage bytes; non_object_root_is_corrupt keeps asserting the empty store for an array root and additionally asserts the sibling holds the original "[1, 2, 3]" bytes. CAUTION: these two pins change expectations by design — the review must confirm the empty-defaults assertions survived intact, not just that the suite is green. A new pin (or an extension of corrupt_store_file_is_quarantined_aside_not_overwritten) proves a missing store file produces no .corrupt sibling, and that after a quarantined load a subsequent save writes a fresh store at the canonical path while the quarantined evidence bytes stay untouched.

Module markup: the SCOPE/CONTRACT quarantine sentence from T-001's markup criterion is finalized here and the dated CHANGE_SUMMARY entry names the quarantine sibling, the two new markers and the honest-evidence rationale; no schema change to profile content — the four lastSession* keys and every other key keep their value shapes, and no migration or new pref key is introduced.

T-004.Title: M-011 bounded close-wait: the quit/window-close prepareCommit races the session write against a fixed two-second bound and proceeds honestly on timeout or rejection

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Failing-first proof precedes implementation: the document-operations pins below are added and shown red on the baseline (today's unbounded await commits only after an arbitrarily slow write and never completes for a never-settling one) before the bounded wait lands.

CAUTION — owner-confirmable value: the bound is a module-level constant in src/renderer/src/store/editor.js, SESSION_COMMIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 2000, with a comment recording it as the C-SESSION-WRITE-ATOMICITY owner-confirmable proposal (consistent with the 400 ms debounce and typical prefs write latency); the owner's confirmation or adjustment is recorded before implementation starts, and any owner-amended value replaces the constant without changing the mechanism.

The deps factory's prepareCommit arm for quit/window-close kinds wraps _saveSessionState in a bounded race: the write promise races a setTimeout(SESSION_COMMIT_TIMEOUT_MS) timer; write settled before the timer → close proceeds with the write's outcome (success: proceed; rejection: log the renderer console marker [Session][close][BLOCK_SESSION_WRITE_FAILED ...] and still proceed — a rejected session write completes the close with the failure surfaced); timer won → the marker [Session][close][BLOCK_SESSION_COMMIT_TIMEOUT bound=2000ms] (or the owner-amended bound) is logged, the timer is cleared, and the close proceeds while the in-flight write is left to settle in the background where the single-transaction backend keeps the previous complete generation on disk. Markers use the existing BLOCK_* console convention; no query text, document contents or absolute user paths in marker fields. The bound exists in the renderer wiring only — documentOperations.js (read-only anchor) keeps awaiting prepareCommit as today, and the m001 close state machine, prevent_close handoff and mt_close_window destroy are unchanged. Non-close kinds keep the exact current prepareCommit behavior (per-owner position flushes, unbounded).

Failing-first renderer pins in tests/renderer/util/document-operations.test.js driving the REAL store wiring (setupTestPinia pattern; documentOperations.js itself stays read-only, so the pins exercise the actual deps factory, not a copy): close_waits_for_session_write_confirmation_before_destroy — with clean tabs and a stubbed still-pending ipcPrefs.setMany, REQUEST_DOCUMENT_OPERATION({kind:'window-close', commit: spy}) does NOT invoke the commit (the close command) before the write settles, and invokes it exactly once after the write resolves; bounded_timeout_still_closes_honestly — with a never-settling setMany the commit is invoked within the fixed bound (the pin exercises the real default bound once; generous waitFor timeout above the bound) and the honest timeout marker is recorded (console.warn spy), the window not left hanging; rejected_session_write_still_closes — with a rejecting setMany the commit is invoked and the failure marker recorded. The existing document-operation pins (admission, barriers, composition checks, version guards) keep passing unweakened — their hand-built deps mock is untouched, so their prepareCommit stays the plain vi.fn(async () => {}).

Session behavior preservation pins stay green: the snapshot content through the batch is shape-identical to the four-key payload, the boot gate and debounce pins keep passing, and no new marker, store field or UI surface appears beyond the two close-path console markers.
